segments.narration: Sixty tonnes of iron fell here and left no crater. A plough hit it in 1920, on a farm outside Grootfontein, Namibia.
Jacobus Brits heard metal screech under his blade. Underneath sat a slab nearly three metres across, eighty-four percent iron, sixteen percent nickel.
So where is the crater? Something this heavy should have punched a hole visible from the air. The ground is flat.
Its flat shape is the answer. The atmosphere braked it from over ten kilometres a second down to roughly two point seven.
It landed hard but not explosively, so it stayed whole. It fell under eighty thousand years ago and has never once been moved from the spot.

verdicts.claim: The atmosphere slowed the object from typical entry speeds above 10 km/s to a terminal velocity of roughly 2.75 km/s.

verdicts.claim: Because it hit at terminal velocity it stayed intact and excavated very little; the fall is estimated at less than 80,000 years ago and the mass has never been moved from the site.
